V ideo game Trainers competed using [Ranked Battle Series 12 Double Battle GS Cup Rules](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/bring-two-restricted-pokemon-into-ranked-battles-series-12-now-under-way/). # 2022 Pokémon World Championships VGC Masters Division

V ideo game Trainers competed using [Ranked Battle Series 12 Double Battle GS Cup Rules](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/bring-two-restricted-pokemon-into-ranked-battles-series-12-now-under-way/). Battles took place in _Pokémon Sword_ and _Pokémon Shield_. Players were permitted to use any Pokémon in the Galar Pokédex, the Isle of Armor Pokédex, and the Crown Tundra Pokédex, as well as certain other Pokémon. Trainers were also allowed to include on their teams two Legendary Pokémon that are usually not permitted in competitive matches.

## 2018 Pokémon World Championships - Video Game Masters Division

Congratulations to the World Champions and to everyone who competed in Nashville, Tennessee at the [2018 Pokémon Video Game World Championships.](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/about/)

Trainers competed using the [2018 VGC format](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/battle-using-the-2018-pokemon-video-game-championships-format/). Battles took place in _Pokémon Ultra Sun_ and _Pokémon Ultra Moon_. Players were permitted to use any Pokémon except for Mythical Pokémon and the most powerful Legendary Pokémon. Don’t forget to check out the [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/vgc-seniors/) and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/vgc-juniors/) Division teams, as well as the [Masters](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-masters/), [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-seniors/), and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-juniors/) Division decks from the Pokémon Trading Card Game event.

## 2018 Pokémon World Championships - Video Game Masters Division

Congratulations to the World Champions and to everyone who competed in Nashville, Tennessee at the [2018 Pokémon Video Game World Championships.](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/about/)

Trainers competed using the [2018 VGC format](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/battle-using-the-2018-pokemon-video-game-championships-format/). Battles took place in _Pokémon Ultra Sun_ and _Pokémon Ultra Moon_. Players were permitted to use any Pokémon except for Mythical Pokémon and the most powerful Legendary Pokémon. Don’t forget to check out the [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/vgc-seniors/) and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/vgc-juniors/) Division teams, as well as the [Masters](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-masters/), [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-seniors/), and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2018/tcg-juniors/) Division decks from the Pokémon Trading Card Game event.

**Incineroar** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ガオガエン**_Gaogaen_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Dark](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dark_(type) "Dark (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Torracat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Torracat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Torracat (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 34. It is the final form of [Litten](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Litten_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Litten (Pokémon)").

## Biology

[![Image 34](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/6/68/Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg/250px-Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg)

[Concept art](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Concept_art_from_Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon "a:Category:Concept art from Pokémon Sun and Moon") featuring Incineroar from [Pokémon Sun and Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon "Pokémon Sun and Moon")

Incineroar is a [humanoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/humanoid "wp:humanoid")[feline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/feline "wp:feline")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a muscular build. It has a short snout with a small red nose, bright green eyes with yellow sclerae, and tiny, pointed ears. Large tufts of red fur extend from its cheeks, and much of its face is also red. The upper half of its muzzle and the top and back of its head are black. A thin red stripe runs vertically along its head to its snout, where it splits into a V-shape over its eyes. Its torso is gray with several black stripes and seems to resemble a wrestler's tank top; the front and back both have a single vertical stripe up the center, crossed by two horizontal lines. Around Incineroar's waist is a belt formed from flames that somewhat resembles a championship wrestling belt. In the front center is a small, yellow flame shape. The arms, legs, and tail are all red with black stripes forming bands around them. The arms have three stripes, spiky tufts of black fur over the shoulders, and large five-fingered hands with white claws and a single light red pad on the palm. Its legs have only two stripes and simple three-toed paws, and the tail has one stripe and a tuft of spiky black fur around the tip.

Incineroar's flame belt is produced from within its body and bursts from its navel and waist as its fighting spirit rises. In addition to spewing fire from its navel, it uses ferocious kicks and punches. Incineroar is an expert on no-holds-barred battles. The flames from its navel can reach a temperature of up to 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit. This Pokémon disregards the safety of its opponents and on-lookers, sometimes striking the opposing Trainer with attacks. Incineroar usually attacks first by unleashing ferocious punches and flinging furious kicks, and then it finishes the opponent by spewing fire from its navel. It is a violent Pokémon with rough, aggressive, and egotistical behavior. It will sometimes ignore its Trainer's orders when it is not in the mood to listen. Despite this, it finds fighting unworthy opponents boring and gets motivated to fight a challenging one. Weak or injured opponents also cause them to lose the desire to fight, which others sometimes use to their advantage.

It also values the attention of the crowd as Incineroar's spirit goes up while the crowd is excited or falters when the crowd is bored. When Incineroar's fighting spirit rises, so does the temperature around its navel waist. While it tends to act like a [heel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/heel_(professional_wrestling) "wp:heel (professional wrestling)"), Incineroar is very happy internally when receiving the admiration of children or young Pokémon.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Incineroar_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) It is also willing to help out children and small Pokémon, further showing its hidden soft side.

In [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII"), [Darkest Lariat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Darkest_Lariat_(move) "Darkest Lariat (move)") was its signature move.

Incineroar is the [only known Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move") capable of using the [Z-Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Z-Move "Z-Move")[Malicious Moonsault](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Malicious_Moonsault_(move) "Malicious Moonsault (move)").

Incineroar evolves from [Torracat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Torracat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Torracat (Pokémon)") and is the final form of [Litten](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Litten_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Litten (Pokémon)").

**Incineroar** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **ガオガエン**_Gaogaen_) is a dual-type [Fire](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Fire_(type) "Fire (type)")/[Dark](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Dark_(type) "Dark (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII").

It [evolves](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") from [Torracat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Torracat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Torracat (Pokémon)") starting at [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") 34. It is the final form of [Litten](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Litten_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Litten (Pokémon)").

## Biology

[![Image 34](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/6/68/Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg/250px-Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Incineroar_SM_concept_art.jpg)

[Concept art](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Concept_art_from_Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon "a:Category:Concept art from Pokémon Sun and Moon") featuring Incineroar from [Pokémon Sun and Moon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon "Pokémon Sun and Moon")

Incineroar is a [humanoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/humanoid "wp:humanoid")[feline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/feline "wp:feline")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a muscular build. It has a short snout with a small red nose, bright green eyes with yellow sclerae, and tiny, pointed ears. Large tufts of red fur extend from its cheeks, and much of its face is also red. The upper half of its muzzle and the top and back of its head are black. A thin red stripe runs vertically along its head to its snout, where it splits into a V-shape over its eyes. Its torso is gray with several black stripes and seems to resemble a wrestler's tank top; the front and back both have a single vertical stripe up the center, crossed by two horizontal lines. Around Incineroar's waist is a belt formed from flames that somewhat resembles a championship wrestling belt. In the front center is a small, yellow flame shape. The arms, legs, and tail are all red with black stripes forming bands around them. The arms have three stripes, spiky tufts of black fur over the shoulders, and large five-fingered hands with white claws and a single light red pad on the palm. Its legs have only two stripes and simple three-toed paws, and the tail has one stripe and a tuft of spiky black fur around the tip.

Incineroar's flame belt is produced from within its body and bursts from its navel and waist as its fighting spirit rises. In addition to spewing fire from its navel, it uses ferocious kicks and punches. Incineroar is an expert on no-holds-barred battles. The flames from its navel can reach a temperature of up to 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit. This Pokémon disregards the safety of its opponents and on-lookers, sometimes striking the opposing Trainer with attacks. Incineroar usually attacks first by unleashing ferocious punches and flinging furious kicks, and then it finishes the opponent by spewing fire from its navel. It is a violent Pokémon with rough, aggressive, and egotistical behavior. It will sometimes ignore its Trainer's orders when it is not in the mood to listen. Despite this, it finds fighting unworthy opponents boring and gets motivated to fight a challenging one. Weak or injured opponents also cause them to lose the desire to fight, which others sometimes use to their advantage.

It also values the attention of the crowd as Incineroar's spirit goes up while the crowd is excited or falters when the crowd is bored. When Incineroar's fighting spirit rises, so does the temperature around its navel waist. While it tends to act like a [heel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/heel_(professional_wrestling) "wp:heel (professional wrestling)"), Incineroar is very happy internally when receiving the admiration of children or young Pokémon.[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Incineroar_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#cite_note-1) It is also willing to help out children and small Pokémon, further showing its hidden soft side.

In [Generation VII](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_VII "Generation VII"), [Darkest Lariat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Darkest_Lariat_(move) "Darkest Lariat (move)") was its signature move.

Incineroar is the [only known Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Signature_move "Signature move") capable of using the [Z-Move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Z-Move "Z-Move")[Malicious Moonsault](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Malicious_Moonsault_(move) "Malicious Moonsault (move)").

### Evolution

Incineroar evolves from [Torracat](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Torracat_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Torracat (Pokémon)") and is the final form of [Litten](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Litten_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Litten (Pokémon)").

(For specifics on this Pokémon's Evolution in the games, refer to [Game data→Evolution data](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Incineroar_(Pok%C3%A9mon)#Evolution_data).)

**Pachirisu** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **パチリス**_Pachirisu_) is an [Electric-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Electric_(type) "Electric (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation IV](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IV "Generation IV").

It is not known to [evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") into or from any other Pokémon.

Along with [Starly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Starly_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Starly (Pokémon)") and [Munchlax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Munchlax_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Munchlax (Pokémon)"), Pachirisu is one of the three [Partner Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Partner_Pok%C3%A9mon_(Ranger) "Partner Pokémon (Ranger)") of [Almia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Almia "Almia") available at the beginning of [Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ranger:_Shadows_of_Almia "Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia").

## Biology

Pachirisu is a small, white squirrel-like [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a faint blueish tint and a light blue stripe starting from its forehead and goes all the way down to the tip of the tail. A female Pachirisu's blue stripe is shorter than a male's. A large white tooth grows out of its mouth. It has deep gray eyes and a yellow circle on each cheek. Its tail is almost twice as big as its body, with three spikes at the top of the curl, which it can use to shoot charges. Though its arms and legs are very short, it can run incredibly fast, enabling it to tire pursuing Pokémon out quickly. It has a great amount of electricity flowing within its body. If it builds up enough charge, it may shock other Pokémon. It is related to the [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)") line.

When it sleeps, Pachirisu likes to curl its big, fluffy tail round to the front of its body and uses it as a pillow. It also likes to chase and groom its tail. When a Pachirisu sheds its fur it shapes them into furballs, which have static charges just like its fur. It hides its favorite [foods](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_food "Pokémon food")—which mainly consist of berries—in these static puffs and stores them in tree holes. It does this to protect the food; if a human or another Pokémon tries to take the food, they will get shocked from the static. It may rub cheek pouches with another Pachirisu to share stored electricity. It is generally found in treetops in forests, as well as the outskirts of a forest and near power plants.

**Pachirisu** ([Japanese](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/List_of_Japanese_Pok%C3%A9mon_names "List of Japanese Pokémon names"): **パチリス**_Pachirisu_) is an [Electric-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Electric_(type) "Electric (type)")[Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") introduced in [Generation IV](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_IV "Generation IV").

It is not known to [evolve](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Evolution "Evolution") into or from any other Pokémon.

Along with [Starly](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Starly_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Starly (Pokémon)") and [Munchlax](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Munchlax_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Munchlax (Pokémon)"), Pachirisu is one of the three [Partner Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Partner_Pok%C3%A9mon_(Ranger) "Partner Pokémon (Ranger)") of [Almia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Almia "Almia") available at the beginning of [Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ranger:_Shadows_of_Almia "Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia").

## Biology

Pachirisu is a small, white squirrel-like [Pokémon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(species) "Pokémon (species)") with a faint blueish tint and a light blue stripe starting from its forehead and goes all the way down to the tip of the tail. A female Pachirisu's blue stripe is shorter than a male's. A large white tooth grows out of its mouth. It has deep gray eyes and a yellow circle on each cheek. Its tail is almost twice as big as its body, with three spikes at the top of the curl, which it can use to shoot charges. Though its arms and legs are very short, it can run incredibly fast, enabling it to tire pursuing Pokémon out quickly. It has a great amount of electricity flowing within its body. If it builds up enough charge, it may shock other Pokémon. It is related to the [Pikachu](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pikachu_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Pikachu (Pokémon)") line.

When it sleeps, Pachirisu likes to curl its big, fluffy tail round to the front of its body and uses it as a pillow. It also likes to chase and groom its tail. When a Pachirisu sheds its fur it shapes them into furballs, which have static charges just like its fur. It hides its favorite [foods](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_food "Pokémon food")—which mainly consist of berries—in these static puffs and stores them in tree holes. It does this to protect the food; if a human or another Pokémon tries to take the food, they will get shocked from the static. It may rub cheek pouches with another Pachirisu to share stored electricity. It is generally found in treetops in forests, as well as the outskirts of a forest and near power plants.

# 2019 Pokémon World Championships - Video Game Masters Division

Congratulations to the World Champions and to everyone who competed in Washington, D.C. at the [2019 Pokémon World Championships](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/about/). Trainers competed using the [2019 VGC Ultra Series](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/get-ready-for-a-legendary-video-game-championships-season/) format. Battles took place in _Pokémon Ultra Sun_ and _Pokémon Ultra Moon_. Players were permitted to use any Pokémon except for Mythical Pokémon, and were limited to two of the most powerful Legendary Pokémon. Don’t forget to check out the [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/vgc-senior/) and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/vgc-junior/) Division teams, as well as the [Masters](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-masters/), [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-senior/), and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-junior/) Division decks from the Pokémon Trading Card Game event.

# 2019 Pokémon World Championships - Video Game Masters Division

Congratulations to the World Champions and to everyone who competed in Washington, D.C. at the [2019 Pokémon World Championships](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/about/). Trainers competed using the [2019 VGC Ultra Series](https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/get-ready-for-a-legendary-video-game-championships-season/) format. Battles took place in _Pokémon Ultra Sun_ and _Pokémon Ultra Moon_. Players were permitted to use any Pokémon except for Mythical Pokémon, and were limited to two of the most powerful Legendary Pokémon. Don’t forget to check out the [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/vgc-senior/) and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/vgc-junior/) Division teams, as well as the [Masters](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-masters/), [Senior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-senior/), and [Junior](https://www.pokemon.com/us/play-pokemon/worlds/2019/tcg-junior/) Division decks from the Pokémon Trading Card Game event.

We all have a least-favorite Pokemon. Mine's Binacle – I don't know exactly why, but something about the Gen 6 barnacle 'mon just doesn't spark joy. However, it's not often that our least favorites become an intrinsic part of our image, but that's something that's about to be etched into Pokemon history permanently for 2016 world champ Wolfe "Wolfey" Glick and his Incineroar.

Wolfey does not like Incineroar. While not his absolute least-favorite 'mon (he previously called it his ["fourth most hated"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XZMaxPmh4Pk)), he's criticized the Alolan starter for decreasing Pokemon diversity in the competitive scene, thanks to its high utility with its Fire/Dark typing and Intimidate ability. Needless to say, it's a very, _very_ good Pokemon, and one that, despite his hatred, has become a mainstay of many of Wolfey's competitive teams, including in the recent Pokemon European International Championships, [which he won](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/pokemon/legendary-pokemon-player-brings-back-his-most-infamous-strategy-for-another-massive-tournament-win-i-dont-think-ive-ever-lost-a-tournament-with-perish/).


This love-hate relationship between Wolfey and Incineroar has been a meme for some time now. The two are permanently associated, and whether he likes it or not, the wrestling cat is probably his signature Pokemon. Now, [The Pokemon Company](https://www.gamesradar.com/tag/the-pokemon-company/) itself has made it official.

Latest Videos From GamesRadar+

Watch full video here:

It's [been revealed](https://www.pokemon.com/uk/play-pokemon/internationals/2025/north-america/pokemon-rewards) that during the 2025 North America International Championships next month, if you tune into the official livestream, you'll be able to get a Mystery Gift distribution password to claim a special "Wolfe Glick's Incineroar" in [Pokemon Scarlet and Violet](https://www.gamesradar.com/pokemon-scarlet-and-violet-guide/). The big cat will have the same moves and stats as Wolfey's during the European International Championships, and as [Serebii reports](https://www.serebii.net/), it should also come with the Partner Ribbon, which will allow you to send it into battle as "Wolfe's Incineroar."

Beyond cementing Wolfey's Incineroar into official Pokemon event history forever (as many other competitive players' signature team members have been in the past), the whole thing is extra amusing since Serebii owner Joe Merrick spoke the idea into existence back in 2023.

We all have a least-favorite Pokemon. Mine's Binacle – I don't know exactly why, but something about the Gen 6 barnacle 'mon just doesn't spark joy. However, it's not often that our least favorites become an intrinsic part of our image, but that's something that's about to be etched into Pokemon history permanently for 2016 world champ Wolfe "Wolfey" Glick and his Incineroar.

Wolfey does not like Incineroar. While not his absolute least-favorite 'mon (he previously called it his ["fourth most hated"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XZMaxPmh4Pk)), he's criticized the Alolan starter for decreasing Pokemon diversity in the competitive scene, thanks to its high utility with its Fire/Dark typing and Intimidate ability. Needless to say, it's a very, _very_ good Pokemon, and one that, despite his hatred, has become a mainstay of many of Wolfey's competitive teams, including in the recent Pokemon European International Championships, [which he won](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/pokemon/legendary-pokemon-player-brings-back-his-most-infamous-strategy-for-another-massive-tournament-win-i-dont-think-ive-ever-lost-a-tournament-with-perish/).


This love-hate relationship between Wolfey and Incineroar has been a meme for some time now. The two are permanently associated, and whether he likes it or not, the wrestling cat is probably his signature Pokemon. Now, [The Pokemon Company](https://www.gamesradar.com/tag/the-pokemon-company/) itself has made it official.

Latest Videos From GamesRadar+

Watch full video here:

It's [been revealed](https://www.pokemon.com/uk/play-pokemon/internationals/2025/north-america/pokemon-rewards) that during the 2025 North America International Championships next month, if you tune into the official livestream, you'll be able to get a Mystery Gift distribution password to claim a special "Wolfe Glick's Incineroar" in [Pokemon Scarlet and Violet](https://www.gamesradar.com/pokemon-scarlet-and-violet-guide/). The big cat will have the same moves and stats as Wolfey's during the European International Championships, and as [Serebii reports](https://www.serebii.net/), it should also come with the Partner Ribbon, which will allow you to send it into battle as "Wolfe's Incineroar."

Beyond cementing Wolfey's Incineroar into official Pokemon event history forever (as many other competitive players' signature team members have been in the past), the whole thing is extra amusing since Serebii owner Joe Merrick spoke the idea into existence back in 2023.

# Teams and Results from the 2022 World Championships

*   [August 22, 2022](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/22/)

![Image 4](https://victoryroad.pro/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/2022-worlds-720.jpg)

| Event | 2022 World Championships |
| --- | --- |
| Location | ![Image 5: GBR](https://victoryroad.pro/wp-content/uploads/flags/GBR-flag.png) London, United Kingdom |
| Date | 18–21 August 2022 |
| Attendance | 307 players |
| Videogame | _Pokémon Sword_ and _Pokémon Shield_ |
| Season | [2022 Season](https://victoryroad.pro/2022-season-events/)– [VGC Series 12](https://victoryroad.pro/2020-season/) |
| Format | 8 Day 1 Swiss rounds + 7 Day 2 Swiss rounds + X-2 Top Cut |

Check out our preview articles on the participating players from [North America](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/16/worlds-meet-na/), [Europe](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/16/worlds-meet-europe/), [Latin America](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/16/worlds-meet-latam/), [Oceania](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/15/worlds-meet-oceania/), [Japan](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/15/worlds-meet-japan/) and the [rest of Asia](https://victoryroad.pro/2022/08/16/worlds-meet-asia/)!

# 2023 Pokémon World Championships VGC Masters Division

P okémon VGC players at the 2023 Pokémon World Championships in Yokohama, Japan, competed using Regulation Set D. Battles took place in the _Pokémon Scarlet_ and _Pokémon Violet_ games. Players were permitted to use all Pokémon available in the Paldea Pokédex—except for Koraidon and Miraidon—as well as certain Pokémon transferred from Pokémon HOME.

# 2023 Pokémon World Championships VGC Masters Division

P okémon VGC players at the 2023 Pokémon World Championships in Yokohama, Japan, competed using Regulation Set D. Battles took place in the _Pokémon Scarlet_ and _Pokémon Violet_ games. Players were permitted to use all Pokémon available in the Paldea Pokédex—except for Koraidon and Miraidon—as well as certain Pokémon transferred from Pokémon HOME.

The **Pokémon World Championships** is an invite-only [trading card game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trading_card_game "Trading card game") and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports") event organized by **Play! Pokémon**. It is held annually in August and features games from the _[Pokémon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon "Pokémon")_ series, including the _[Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Trading\_Card\_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game")_, [_Pokémon_ video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(video_game_series) "Pokémon (video game series)") and _[Pokémon Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Go "Pokémon Go")_. Players earn invitations to the World Championships based on their performance in qualifiers and other tournaments held throughout the season and compete for scholarship money, prizes and the title of World Champion. With the exception of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"), invitations to the World Championships are administered by the Play! Pokémon program.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Pokémon World Championships first began with the [Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") (TCG) in 2004, which was around the time that the franchise was regaining its popularity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-7) In 2008, Play! Pokémon began to organize competitive tournaments for the _Pokémon_ video game series alongside the TCG, which is collectively known as the Video Game Championships (VGC). Like the TCG Championships, players compete with other players in their own age divisions (i.e. Junior, Senior and Masters) in different Premier Tournaments, and the season culminates with the best players earning an invitation to play the Pokémon World Championships in August. The tournaments in VGC were played with a different game each year, mainly the latest _Pokémon_ game from its main series, up until 2025. From 2026, all VGC tournaments will be played on _[Pokémon Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Champions "Pokémon Champions")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-8)

In 2013, the Pokémon World Championships marked the first time the tournament would be held outside the usual United States. It took place inside [Vancouver Convention Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Convention_Centre "Vancouver Convention Centre") in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") of [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"). The 2015 Championships marked the first tournament to feature a spin-off game in the current tournament rotation, with _[Pokkén Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n\_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament")_ being included in the list.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-9) In 2018, the upper _Pokkén Tournament DX_ was used instead. 2019 added its second addition of a spin-off game series into rotation, _[Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_GO "Pokémon GO")_.

The 2020 tournament marked the second time the tournament was hosted outside United States, and the first outside the [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") continent. It was announced to be held at [Excel London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excel_London "Excel London") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), United Kingdom.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-:0-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-:1-11) This is likely due to the setting of _[Pokémon Sword and Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Sword\_and\_Shield "Pokémon Sword and Shield")_, which takes place in a region inspired by the United Kingdom known as Galar, and it is the set of games that would be played by the video game division of the Pokémon World Championships.

The 2020 tournament was originally planned to be held in 2020, but on March 31 that year, in-light with the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the tournament was postponed with its 2020 seasons being suspended,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-13) which proceeds from earlier announcements in March which saw the cancellation of the 2020 European International Championships[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-15) and part of its season between March and June 2020.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-17) The tournament was not held in 2021 following another postponement on February 9, 2021, and that tournament ultimately held on August 18-21, 2022.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-18)

Prior to the 2022 series, in early January 2022, Play! Pokémon announced the inclusion of a third spin-off game into the competition lineup, _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_; four months later, it was announced the _Pokkén Tournament_ would host its last season, thus rotating the latter game out of tournament lineup from 2023 onwards. It marked the newest [MOBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOBA "MOBA") game to have an official esports tournament, after _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_.

The 2023 Pokémon World Championships marked its third tournament to be held outside United States, the first time to be hosted in their franchise's country of origin, and the first in the Asian region, at the [Pacifico Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacifico_Yokohama "Pacifico Yokohama") in [Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokohama "Yokohama"), Japan (the basis of Vermilion City in the Kanto region). After the PWC ended, The Pokémon Company announced that the Pokémon World Championships would return to [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii") for the first time since the previous World Championships in the state was held back in 2012.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-PWC_24-19) Both the 2025 and 2026 events were held at the state of [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), in [Anaheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California") and [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), respectively. The 2026 tournament marked the first time where two separate venues were used for the tournament, with one for the main event and another, [Chase Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Center "Chase Center"), would serve as the venue for the Championship Sunday.

At the conclusion of the 2026 event, it was announced that [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") would host the 2027 event, marking the return of the tournament to Asia for the first time since the 2023 event in Yokohama and the first time [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") is given the hosting rights, and the fourth overall outside United States.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-20) The tournament rules and season lineup were published on September 8, and also announced that _Pokémon Unite_ is rotated out from the tournament rotation. Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese languages for the commentary will also be added towards the current languages for the commentaries.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-PWC2027Regulation-21)

## Qualification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Qualification")]

The qualifying process for the Pokémon World Championships varies each year and is dependent on a player's age division and the country in which they are located in. Players may also qualify to play on different days of the World Championships based on their performance in their respective qualifying programs; the best performing players will immediately advance to the second day of the World Championships playoffs (i.e. "Day 2") instead of playing through the first day (i.e. "Day 1").

### Play! Pokémon program

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Play! Pokémon program")]

Players located in a country with a Play! Pokémon program (i.e. in [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America"), [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe"), [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania")) compete in a regular schedule of tournaments for Championship Points and receive invitations when they meet a predetermined threshold of points at the end of the season.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-39)

In 2015, the Play! Pokémon program expanded to include countries from the continents of [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") (except Japan and South Korea). However, on June 10, 2020, it was announced that [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") would no longer be part of the Play! Pokémon program and will have its own qualifying system towards the Pokémon World Championships.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-40)

### Pokémon GO Championship Series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Pokémon GO Championship Series")]

Pokémon announced in October 2021 that [Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Go "Pokémon Go") would be added during the 2022 World Championships,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-42) along with it a qualification system through the Pokémon GO Championship Series, where the top two head to the World Championships.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-43) Any trainer who reached Legend rank during Season 9 of the [Pokémon GO Battle League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_9 "Pokémon GO Battle League") would qualify for the GO Championship Series.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-44)

#### 2022 Championship Series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022 Championship Series")]

The 2022 [Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO") Championship Series is a series with a purpose of acting as a qualification system to the 2022 Pokémon World Championship.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-45) The series consists of events spread throughout the globe.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) The series is divided into the Senior's and Master's divisions.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) The series' format revolves around the Great League.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) Players can enter the championship either by attaining Legend rank during either [Season 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_9 "Pokémon GO Battle League") or [Season 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_10 "Pokémon GO Battle League") of the GO Battle League, or by registering via Play! Pokémon after the Legend-rank registration closes.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47) Every event is divided between a regional or international event. The top Pokémon players at these events would be given an invitation to the 2022 World Championship.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47) The earliest event began on 26 March, in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool"), with the latest being on 24 June, in [Columbus, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47)

### Pokémon Unite Championship Series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Pokémon Unite Championship Series")]

See also: [_Pokémon Unite_ § In esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Unite#In_esports "Pokémon Unite")

In January 2022, _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_ producer Masaaki Hoshino confirmed that the game would be part of the roster of games to be played at the World Championships in London.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-48) For the first season of the Pokémon Unite Championship Series, there will be eleven supported Regional Zones: North America, Central America, South America-East, South America-West, Europe, Oceania, Japan, South Korea, India, and the Asia-Pacific region. These events will only be open to players aged 16 or 18, depending on the region or country they are from.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-49)

In each month, a series of tournaments in each Regional Zone will be held. Like other games in the World Championships, players will earn Championship Points based on their finishing position in that month's tournament. The CP can be retained by players to allow for team changes as the season carries on. The team with the most points qualifies for the Regional Championships, and the top teams from the Regional Championships qualify for a chance to compete at the Pokémon World Championships.

In January 2023, there were changes to the competitive structure and Regional Zones. Pokémon World Championships nearly doubled available spots from 16, to 31 teams. Regional Zones controlled by TPCi were also changed, with Central America, South America-East and South America West being changed to LATAM North, LATAM South, and Brazil. TPC had also taken control of the India and Asia-Pacific Regional Zones, and split Asia-Pacific into 2 regions; Asia-Pacific East and Asia-Pacific West. For TPCi controlled regions, the previous month's top 4 did not auto qualify for the next month's tournament finals. Additionally, an extra monthly tournament was added, the April Cup. Championship Points were also changed to include top CP earners an invite to Pokémon World Championships, ranging from top 1 to 3 in top CP earners depending on how many invites were given for a region. For TPC controlled regions, their tournament circuit began in April, with 3 monthly qualifiers. The winners of these qualifiers then participated in Regionals to earn a spot for Pokémon World Championships.

Among those changes, both North America and Europe were also given their first regional LAN event. Europe had a LAN event for their Aeos Cup series at European International Championships. North America were given a regional LAN event at the North America International Championships.

In 2023, competing countries were divided into eight groups of four teams (groups A to H). Teams in each group play each another in a best-of-three series [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), with the top team advancing to the Top 8 knockout stage. The final draw took place virtually on the _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_[YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on July 28, 2023. The prize pool was $500,000 in USD and was distributed among the Top 16 finishers in the championship.

### Japan & South Korea

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Japan & South Korea")]

Tournaments in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea") are organized independently from Play! Pokémon, and as such, players from these countries have a different system of qualification.

In Japan, players compete for an invite to the _Japan National Championships_ by playing in major qualifier or online tournaments held throughout the season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-51) The best performing players of the _Japan National Championships_ will then be selected to represent Japan in the Pokémon World Championships.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-52)

In South Korea, the style of qualification for the World Championships changes frequently. For example, in 2015, players would compete in the _Korean National Championships_ and earn a World Championships invitation based on their standing in the tournament. However, in 2019, players would compete in tournaments organized by the _Korean League_ and earn an invite based on the number of points they had accumulated by the end of the season.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-53)

### Other

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Other")]

There are other less common methods of qualifying for the World Championships which include finishing at least top 4 or better in the prior year's World Championships or by participating in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") known as the Last Chance Qualifier[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-54) at the location of the World Championships itself.

Washington Convention Center on [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. The **Pokémon World Championships** is an invite-only [trading card game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trading_card_game "Trading card game") and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports") event organized by **Play! Pokémon**. It is held annually in August and features games from the _[Pokémon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon "Pokémon")_ series, including the _[Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Trading\_Card\_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game")_, [_Pokémon_ video games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_(video_game_series) "Pokémon (video game series)") and _[Pokémon Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Go "Pokémon Go")_. Players earn invitations to the World Championships based on their performance in qualifiers and other tournaments held throughout the season and compete for scholarship money, prizes and the title of World Champion. With the exception of [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia"), invitations to the World Championships are administered by the Play! Pokémon program.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Pokémon World Championships first began with the [Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") (TCG) in 2004, which was around the time that the franchise was regaining its popularity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-7) In 2008, Play! Pokémon began to organize competitive tournaments for the _Pokémon_ video game series alongside the TCG, which is collectively known as the Video Game Championships (VGC). Like the TCG Championships, players compete with other players in their own age divisions (i.e. Junior, Senior and Masters) in different Premier Tournaments, and the season culminates with the best players earning an invitation to play the Pokémon World Championships in August. The tournaments in VGC were played with a different game each year, mainly the latest _Pokémon_ game from its main series, up until 2025. From 2026, all VGC tournaments will be played on _[Pokémon Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Champions "Pokémon Champions")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-8)

In 2013, the Pokémon World Championships marked the first time the tournament would be held outside the usual United States. It took place inside [Vancouver Convention Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Convention_Centre "Vancouver Convention Centre") in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver"), [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") of [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"). The 2015 Championships marked the first tournament to feature a spin-off game in the current tournament rotation, with _[Pokkén Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokk%C3%A9n\_Tournament "Pokkén Tournament")_ being included in the list.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-9) In 2018, the upper _Pokkén Tournament DX_ was used instead. 2019 added its second addition of a spin-off game series into rotation, _[Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_GO "Pokémon GO")_.

The 2020 tournament marked the second time the tournament was hosted outside United States, and the first outside the [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") continent. It was announced to be held at [Excel London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excel_London "Excel London") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), United Kingdom.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-:0-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-:1-11) This is likely due to the setting of _[Pokémon Sword and Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Sword\_and\_Shield "Pokémon Sword and Shield")_, which takes place in a region inspired by the United Kingdom known as Galar, and it is the set of games that would be played by the video game division of the Pokémon World Championships.

The 2020 tournament was originally planned to be held in 2020, but on March 31 that year, in-light with the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the tournament was postponed with its 2020 seasons being suspended,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-13) which proceeds from earlier announcements in March which saw the cancellation of the 2020 European International Championships[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-15) and part of its season between March and June 2020.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-17) The tournament was not held in 2021 following another postponement on February 9, 2021, and that tournament ultimately held on August 18-21, 2022.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-18)

Prior to the 2022 series, in early January 2022, Play! Pokémon announced the inclusion of a third spin-off game into the competition lineup, _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_; four months later, it was announced the _Pokkén Tournament_ would host its last season, thus rotating the latter game out of tournament lineup from 2023 onwards. It marked the newest [MOBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOBA "MOBA") game to have an official esports tournament, after _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_.

The 2023 Pokémon World Championships marked its third tournament to be held outside United States, the first time to be hosted in their franchise's country of origin, and the first in the Asian region, at the [Pacifico Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacifico_Yokohama "Pacifico Yokohama") in [Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokohama "Yokohama"), Japan (the basis of Vermilion City in the Kanto region). After the PWC ended, The Pokémon Company announced that the Pokémon World Championships would return to [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii") for the first time since the previous World Championships in the state was held back in 2012.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-PWC_24-19) Both the 2025 and 2026 events were held at the state of [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), in [Anaheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California") and [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), respectively. The 2026 tournament marked the first time where two separate venues were used for the tournament, with one for the main event and another, [Chase Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Center "Chase Center"), would serve as the venue for the Championship Sunday.

At the conclusion of the 2026 event, it was announced that [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") would host the 2027 event, marking the return of the tournament to Asia for the first time since the 2023 event in Yokohama and the first time [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") is given the hosting rights, and the fourth overall outside United States.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-20) The tournament rules and season lineup were published on September 8, and also announced that _Pokémon Unite_ is rotated out from the tournament rotation. Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese languages for the commentary will also be added towards the current languages for the commentaries.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-PWC2027Regulation-21)

## Qualification

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Qualification")]

The qualifying process for the Pokémon World Championships varies each year and is dependent on a player's age division and the country in which they are located in. Players may also qualify to play on different days of the World Championships based on their performance in their respective qualifying programs; the best performing players will immediately advance to the second day of the World Championships playoffs (i.e. "Day 2") instead of playing through the first day (i.e. "Day 1").

### Play! Pokémon program

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Play! Pokémon program")]

Players located in a country with a Play! Pokémon program (i.e. in [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America"), [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe"), [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania")) compete in a regular schedule of tournaments for Championship Points and receive invitations when they meet a predetermined threshold of points at the end of the season.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-39)

In 2015, the Play! Pokémon program expanded to include countries from the continents of [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") (except Japan and South Korea). However, on June 10, 2020, it was announced that [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia") would no longer be part of the Play! Pokémon program and will have its own qualifying system towards the Pokémon World Championships.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-40)

Pokémon announced in October 2021 that [Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Go "Pokémon Go") would be added during the 2022 World Championships,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-42) along with it a qualification system through the Pokémon GO Championship Series, where the top two head to the World Championships.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-43) Any trainer who reached Legend rank during Season 9 of the [Pokémon GO Battle League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_9 "Pokémon GO Battle League") would qualify for the GO Championship Series.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-44)

#### 2022 Championship Series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022 Championship Series")]

The 2022 [Pokémon GO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO "Pokémon GO") Championship Series is a series with a purpose of acting as a qualification system to the 2022 Pokémon World Championship.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-45) The series consists of events spread throughout the globe.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) The series is divided into the Senior's and Master's divisions.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) The series' format revolves around the Great League.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSEvents-46) Players can enter the championship either by attaining Legend rank during either [Season 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_9 "Pokémon GO Battle League") or [Season 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO_Battle_League#Season_10 "Pokémon GO Battle League") of the GO Battle League, or by registering via Play! Pokémon after the Legend-rank registration closes.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47) Every event is divided between a regional or international event. The top Pokémon players at these events would be given an invitation to the 2022 World Championship.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47) The earliest event began on 26 March, in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool"), with the latest being on 24 June, in [Columbus, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-GOCSListEvents-47)

### Pokémon Unite Championship Series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Pokémon Unite Championship Series")]

See also: [_Pokémon Unite_ § In esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Unite#In_esports "Pokémon Unite")

In January 2022, _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_ producer Masaaki Hoshino confirmed that the game would be part of the roster of games to be played at the World Championships in London.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-48) For the first season of the Pokémon Unite Championship Series, there will be eleven supported Regional Zones: North America, Central America, South America-East, South America-West, Europe, Oceania, Japan, South Korea, India, and the Asia-Pacific region. These events will only be open to players aged 16 or 18, depending on the region or country they are from.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-49)

In each month, a series of tournaments in each Regional Zone will be held. Like other games in the World Championships, players will earn Championship Points based on their finishing position in that month's tournament. The CP can be retained by players to allow for team changes as the season carries on. The team with the most points qualifies for the Regional Championships, and the top teams from the Regional Championships qualify for a chance to compete at the Pokémon World Championships.

In January 2023, there were changes to the competitive structure and Regional Zones. Pokémon World Championships nearly doubled available spots from 16, to 31 teams. Regional Zones controlled by TPCi were also changed, with Central America, South America-East and South America West being changed to LATAM North, LATAM South, and Brazil. TPC had also taken control of the India and Asia-Pacific Regional Zones, and split Asia-Pacific into 2 regions; Asia-Pacific East and Asia-Pacific West. For TPCi controlled regions, the previous month's top 4 did not auto qualify for the next month's tournament finals. Additionally, an extra monthly tournament was added, the April Cup. Championship Points were also changed to include top CP earners an invite to Pokémon World Championships, ranging from top 1 to 3 in top CP earners depending on how many invites were given for a region. For TPC controlled regions, their tournament circuit began in April, with 3 monthly qualifiers. The winners of these qualifiers then participated in Regionals to earn a spot for Pokémon World Championships.

Among those changes, both North America and Europe were also given their first regional LAN event. Europe had a LAN event for their Aeos Cup series at European International Championships. North America were given a regional LAN event at the North America International Championships.

In 2023, competing countries were divided into eight groups of four teams (groups A to H). Teams in each group play each another in a best-of-three series [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), with the top team advancing to the Top 8 knockout stage. The final draw took place virtually on the _[Pokémon Unite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon\_Unite "Pokémon Unite")_[YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on July 28, 2023. The prize pool was $500,000 in USD and was distributed among the Top 16 finishers in the championship.

### Japan & South Korea

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Japan & South Korea")]

Tournaments in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea") are organized independently from Play! Pokémon, and as such, players from these countries have a different system of qualification.

In Japan, players compete for an invite to the _Japan National Championships_ by playing in major qualifier or online tournaments held throughout the season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-51) The best performing players of the _Japan National Championships_ will then be selected to represent Japan in the Pokémon World Championships.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-52)

In South Korea, the style of qualification for the World Championships changes frequently. For example, in 2015, players would compete in the _Korean National Championships_ and earn a World Championships invitation based on their standing in the tournament. However, in 2019, players would compete in tournaments organized by the _Korean League_ and earn an invite based on the number of points they had accumulated by the end of the season.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-53)

### Other

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Other")]

There are other less common methods of qualifying for the World Championships which include finishing at least top 4 or better in the prior year's World Championships or by participating in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") known as the Last Chance Qualifier[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_World_Championships#cite_note-54) at the location of the World Championships itself.
